He played [[college basketball]] for two seasons with the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]] before transferring to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], where he earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). In 2026, he won a championship with the [[2026 NBA Finals|Knicks]]. After forgoing his senior year in college to enter the [[2014 NBA draft]], Clarkson was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the second round with the 46th overall pick and was immediately traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]]. He also holds Filipino citizenship and has represented the [[Philippine men's national basketball team|Philippine national team]].{{cite web | url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/2015/08/25/1492076/look-jordan-clarkson-ph-passport | title=Jordan Clarkson PH passport| work=Philippine Star | access-date=August 31, 2015}}{{cite web | url= http://cnnphilippines.com/sports/2015/08/24/Gilas-Pilipinas-Jordan-Clarkson-natural-born.html | title= SBP: No need to naturalize Jordan Clarkson | work= CNN Philippines | access-date= August 31, 2015 | archive-date= October 13, 2016 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20161013125419/http://cnnphilippines.com/sports/2015/08/24/Gilas-Pilipinas-Jordan-Clarkson-natural-born.html | url-status= dead }}{{cite web | url= https://chinapost.nownews.com/20150829-42776 | title= NBA's Jordan Clarkson could visit during Jones Cup | work= China Post | date= August 28, 2015 | access-date= August 31, 2015 | archive-date= August 28, 2018 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180828170429/https://chinapost.nownews.com/20150829-42776 | url-status= dead }} In 2021, Clarkson was named the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/photogallery/clarkson-facts-stats|title=10 Facts and Stats About Jordan Clarkson|website=NBA|date=February 8, 2018}} ==Early life== Clarkson was born in [[Tampa, Florida]], to [[African-American]] Mike Clarkson and [[Filipino Americans|Filipino American]] Annette Tullao Davis. Davis' mother, Marcelina Tullao Kingsolver, was from [[Bacolor]], Pampanga, Philippines.{{cite news|first=Sam|last=Laird|title=Lakers start first Asian-American backcourt in NBA history|date=March 26, 2015|work=Mashable|url=https://mashable.com/2015/03/25/lakers-start-first-asian-american-backcourt-in-nba-history/|access-date=January 18, 2021}}{{Cite web|url=http://sports.abs-cbn.com/nba/news/2017/10/19/jordan-clarkson-s-biggest-fan-his-lola-marcelina-32420|title=Jordan Clarkson's biggest fan? His Lola Marcelina|website=ABS-CBN SPORTS|language=en|access-date=October 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021200828/https://sports.abs-cbn.com/nba/news/2017/10/19/jordan-clarkson-s-biggest-fan-his-lola-marcelina-32420|archive-date=October 21, 2019}}{{Cite web|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/317553/clarksons-dream-deferred-no|title=Clarkson's dream deferred no more|last=Della|first=Percy D.|website=sports.inquirer.net|date=August 31, 2018|language=en|access-date=October 21, 2019}} Both his parents served in the [[United States Air Force]] and divorced when Clarkson was young, with Clarkson's father later remarrying Janie Clarkson.{{Cite web |last=Bresnahan |first=Mike |date=January 4, 2015 |title=Father's diagnosis affected Jordan Clarkson on the court |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-jordan-clarkson-20150104-story.html |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150331/lakers-rookie-jordan-clarkson-finds-inspiration-from-his-father-coach-friend-cancer-survivor|title=Lakers' rookie Jordan Clarkson finds inspiration from his father – coach, friend, cancer survivor|date=April 1, 2015|website=Daily News|language=en-US|access-date=October 21, 2019}} He moved to [[San Antonio, Texas]] around age six.{{cite news |last=Flores |first=David |title=Wagner grad Clarkson makes first NBA start in Lakers' loss to Spurs |date=January 24, 2015 |work=Kens5.com |url=http://www.kens5.com/story/opinion/contributors/david-flores/2015/01/24/wagner-grad-clarkson-makes-first-nba-start-against-spurs/22265519/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150810153714/http://www.kens5.com/story/opinion/contributors/david-flores/2015/01/24/wagner-grad-clarkson-makes-first-nba-start-against-spurs/22265519/ |archive-date=August 10, 2015 |url-status=live }} He attended [[Karen Wagner High School]] in San Antonio. As a sophomore, he averaged 10 points per game while earning honorable mention all-district accolades. As a junior, he averaged 20 points, six rebounds and four assists per game, leading his team to a 32–8 record and the Class 5A state semi-finals.{{cite web | url=http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_clarkson_802288.html | title=Jordan Clarkson Bio | work=MUTigers.com | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612045048/http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_clarkson_802288.html|archive-date=June 12, 2015}} On November 11, 2009, Clarkson signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Tulsa]].{{cite web | url=http://www.tulsahurricane.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111109aab.html | title=Tulsa Basketball Signs Three Prep Seniors | work=TulsaHurricane.com | date=November 11, 2009 | access-date=July 8, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714190149/http://www.tulsahurricane.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111109aab.html | archive-date=July 14, 2014 }} As a senior, he averaged 18.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 2.1 steals, leading his team to a 38–2 record and a semifinal loss in the state championship. He was also named San Antonio High School Player of the Year. ==College career== ===Tulsa=== In his freshman season at [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]], Clarkson was named to the 2011 Conference USA All-Freshman team after being named the Conference USA Freshman of the Week four times in 2010–11. In 27 games (nine starts), he averaged 11.5 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.9 assists in 24.9 minutes per game.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jordan-clarkson-1.html | title=Jordan Clarkson Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=July 8, 2014}} In his sophomore season, he was named to the All-Conference USA first team and the NABC All-District 11 team. In 31 games (all starts), he averaged 16.5 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 33.9 minutes per game. ===Missouri=== [[File:Jordan Clarkson with Missouri in 2014.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Clarkson with [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] in 2014]] In May 2012, Clarkson transferred to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]]{{cite web | url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/18984674/tulsa-transfer-jordan-clarkson-headed-to-missouri | title=Tulsa transfer Jordan Clarkson headed to Missouri | work=CBSSports.com | date=May 7, 2012 | access-date=July 8, 2014}} and subsequently sat out the 2012–13 season due to [[NCAA]] transfer rules. In his [[redshirted]] junior season, he was named to the 2014 All-SEC second team. He was also named to the Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 list in January 2014 and won three [[Southeastern Conference]] Player of the Week honors. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 17.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.1 steals in 35.1 minutes per game. On March 31, 2014, Clarkson declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10701976/missouri-tigers-jordan-clarkson-nba-draft | title=Jordan Clarkson chooses NBA draft | publisher=ESPN | date=March 31, 2014 | access-date=July 8, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2014–2018)=== [[File:Jordan Clarkson vs Otto Porter.jpg|thumb|240px|left|Clarkson dribbles against [[Otto Porter]] in 2015.]] On June 26, 2014, Clarkson was selected with the 46th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]]. He was later traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on draft night for cash considerations,{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140626_clarkson_draftrights | title=Lakers Acquire Draft Rights to Jordan Clarkson | work=NBA.com | date=June 26, 2014 | access-date=July 8, 2014}}{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/140707clarkson_introduced | title=Lakers Introduce Jordan Clarkson | work=NBA.com | date=July 7, 2014 | access-date=July 8, 2014}} and joined the team for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/140701summer_invitees | title=Lakers Announce 2014 Summer League Invitees and Schedule | work=NBA.com | date=July 1, 2014 | access-date=July 8, 2014}} On August 25, 2014, he signed with the Lakers.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140825jordanclarkson_signed | title=Lakers Sign Jordan Clarkson | work=NBA.com | date=August 25, 2014 | access-date=August 25, 2014}} During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]],{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2014–15 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 6, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }} and did not play for the Lakers for most of the first half of the season. However, he ended up starting 38 games for the Lakers, primarily at [[point guard]], and averaged 15.8 points, 5.0 assists, and 4.2 rebounds as a starter.{{cite news |last=Pincus |first=Eric |title=Jordan Clarkson named to NBA all-rookie first team |date=May 18, 2015 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-jordan-clarkson-nba-all-rookie-team-20150518-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150521035744/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-jordan-clarkson-nba-all-rookie-team-20150518-story.html |archive-date=May 21, 2015 |url-status=live }} On March 24, 2015, he had a season-best game with 30 points and 7 assists in a loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150324/LALOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Lakers at Thunder|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113032356/http://www.nba.com/games/20150324/LALOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 13, 2016|url-status=dead}} Starting alongside [[Jeremy Lin]], the pair became the first Asian-American starting backcourt in league history.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SRBU74b6ZAE|title=Lin and Clarkson Become NBA's First Asian-American Starting Backcourt|work=NBA|date=March 25, 2015|via=YouTube}} On March 30 and April 1, Clarkson recorded back-to-back double-doubles. For the season, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]]. In the prior 30 years, there had been only four other second-round picks that were named to the first team.{{cite news |last=Walentik |first=Steve |title=Clarkson named to NBA All-Rookie first team |date=May 18, 2015 |newspaper=Columbia Daily Tribune |url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/22c8ed24-e560-5240-8cc5-0f689e99e586.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107113815/https://www.columbiatribune.com/22c8ed24-e560-5240-8cc5-0f689e99e586.html |archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=live }} Clarkson after joining the Lakers garnered a huge following in the Philippines owing to his Filipino heritage and the existing fanbase of the NBA team in the country.{{cite news |last1=Cacciola |first1=Scott |title=In the Philippines, Everyone Knows Jordan Clarkson's Name |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/05/sports/nba-jazz-jordan-clarkson-philippines.html |access-date=April 5, 2021 |work=The New York web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/as.rising.stars/2016-rising-stars-challenge-event-page/|title=USA downs World in BBVA Rising Stars, LaVine gets MVP|website=[[NBA.com]] }} On July 7, 2016, Clarkson re-signed with the Lakers on a four-year, $50 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160707clarksondengzubac|title=Lakers Sign Clarkson, Deng, and Zubac – Los Angeles Lakers|website=[[NBA.com]] }}{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2016/07/07/the-latest-currys-wife-regrets-calling-nba-rigged/86800200/|title=The Latest: Lakers announce signing Deng, Zubac, Clarkson|website=[[USA Today]] }} In the Lakers' season opener on October 26, 2016, Clarkson scored a team-high 25 points off the bench in a 120–114 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899415|title=Young Lakers roar past Rockets 120–114 to win Walton's debut|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}} On November 15, 2016, he recorded a career-high five steals in a 125–118 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899607|title=Russell, Randle push surging Lakers past Nets, 125–118|work=ESPN.com|date=November 15, 2016|access-date=November 16, 2016}} On March 12, 2017, he tied his career high with 30 points off the bench in a 118–116 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900385|title=Saric, Okafor lead 76ers past Lakers 118–116|work=ESPN.com|date=March 12, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017}} On March 24, 2017, he had career highs of 35 points and eight 3-pointers in a 130–119 overtime win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900475|title=Lakers beat Wolves 130–119 in OT to snap 6-game skid|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=March 25, 2017}} On November 13, 2017, Clarkson scored a season-high 25 points in 26 minutes off the bench in a 100–93 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974947|title=Clarkson scores 25, Lakers beat Suns 100–93|work=ESPN.com|date=November 13, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2017}} On January 19, 2018, he set a new season high with 33 points in a 99–86 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975419|title=Clarkson leads Lakers to 99–86 win over Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2018|access-date=January 19, 2018}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2019)=== [[File:Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Brooklyn Nets (47112577701).jpg|thumb|right|Clarkson with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2019]] On February 8, 2018, Clarkson was traded, along with [[Larry Nance Jr.]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], [[Channing Frye]] and a 2018 first-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Acquire Jordan Clarkson and Larry Nance Jr. From Lakers|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/clarkson-lnance-trade-180208|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2018|date=February 8, 2018}} In his debut for the Cavaliers three days later, Clarkson scored 17 points in a 121–99 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975581|title=Truth is: Cavaliers beat Celtics 121–99 on Paul Pierce's day|work=ESPN.com|date=February 11, 2018|access-date=February 11, 2018}} The Cavaliers reached the [[2018 NBA Finals]], where they were defeated in four games by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On December 12, 2018, Clarkson scored 28 points in a 113–106 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071087|title=Hood's late basket sends Cavs past Knicks 113–106|work=ESPN.com|date=December 12, 2018|access-date=December 27, 2018}} On February 13, 2019, Clarkson scored a career-high 42 points in a 148–139 triple-overtime loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071526|title=Russell scores 36, Nets outlast Cavaliers 148–139 in 3OTs|work=ESPN.com|date=February 13, 2019|access-date=February 14, 2019}} ===Utah Jazz (2019–2025)=== On December 24, 2019, Clarkson was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Dante Exum]] and two future second-round draft picks.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz acquire guard Jordan Clarkson|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-guard-jordan-clarkson|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 24, 2019|date=December 24, 2019}}{{cite Trade|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2019/12/23/21036000/utah-jazz-players-react-to-news-of-dante-exum-trade-cleveland-jazz-get-jordan-clarkson-in-jeff-green|work=Deseret.com|access-date=December 24, 2019|date=December 24, 2019}} On January 30, 2020, Clarkson scored a season-high 37 points in a 100–106 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|last=Todd|first=Sarah|date=January 31, News|language=en}} On November 21, 2020, Clarkson re-signed with the Jazz on a four-year, $52 million contract.{{Cite web|title=Reports: Jazz to sign Derrick Favors, re-sign Jordan Clarkson {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/news/reports-jazz-to-sign-derrick-favors-re-sign-jordan-clarkson|access-date=November 21, 2020|website=NBA.com}} On February 15, 2021, Clarkson scored a season-high 40 points in a 134–123 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/jazz-news-jordan-clarkson-on-outdueling-ben-simmons-with-scintillating-40-point-night/|title=Jazz's Jordan Clarkson on outdueling Ben Simmons with scintillating 40-point night|website=ClutchPoints|last=Cruz|first=Mike|date=February 16, 2021|access-date=February 19, 2021}} He ended the [[2020–21 Utah Jazz season|2020–21 season]] averaging a career-high 18.4 points per game and led the NBA with 203 three-pointers off the bench. He won the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] over Jazz teammate [[Joe Ingles]], who was the runner-up. Clarkson was the first Utah player to win the award.{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Walden|title=Utah Jazz guard Jordan Clarkson wins Sixth Man of the Year award|date=May 25, 2021|newspaper=The Salt Lake Trubune|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2021/05/24/utah-jazz-guard-jordan/|access-date=May 25, 2021}} On October 28, 2021, Clarkson and [[Jalen Green]] became the first two players of Filipino descent to play in the same NBA game in time for the [[Houston Rockets]]' Filipino Heritage Night celebration.{{cite web |last1=Ireland |first1=Kyle |title=Clarkson, Green Become First Two Players Of Filipino Descent To Play In Same NBA Game |url=https://kslsports.com/471155/clarkson-green-become-first-two-players-of-filipino-descent-to-play-in-same-nba-game/ |website=kslsports.com |access-date=January 18, 2023 |date=October 29, 2021}} On March 12, 2022, Clarkson scored a career-high 45 points on 15-for-21 shooting from the field in a 134–125 win against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |title=Clarkson drops career-high 45 as Jazz withstand Fox's 41|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-uta-0022101010|website=NBA.com |language=en |date=March 13, 2022}} On December rebounds.[https://www.cachevalleydaily.com/news/archive/2022/12/16/clarkson-scores-39-points-jazz-outlast-pelicans-in-ot/#.Y8DV0xZMEWM Clarkson scores 39 points, Jazz outlast Pelicans in OT] On January 14, 2023, Clarkson scored 38 points and grabbed 9 rebounds during a 118–117 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468801 Embiid's jumper gives 76ers 118-117 win over Jazz] On July 7, 2023, Clarkson signed a two-year, $28.4 million contract extension with the Jazz, that also included a re-negotiation of his 2023–24 salary, increasing it to $23.5 million.{{Cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Jordan Clarkson to Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-jordan-clarkson-to-contract-extension|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=July 17, 2023|website=NBA.com}} On January 1, 2024, Clarkson recorded his first career triple-double with 20 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 127–90 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], the first in hard work is finally paying off |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5174035/2024/01/02/jordan-clarkson-triple-double-jazz/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=January 2, 2024 |language=en |date=January 2, 2024}} On December 19, 2024, Clarkson was ejected after an altercation with [[Paul Reed (basketball)|Paul Reed]], almost starting an altercation with [[Ron Holland (basketball)|Ron Holland]], and while being ejected, he threw his headband into the crowds. On December 21, he was fined $35,000 for the altercations and headband throwing.{{cite web | url=https://pr.nba.com/jazz-pistons-penalties/ | title=NBA announces penalties from Jazz-Pistons game | date=December 21, 2024 }} In 37 appearances (9 starts) for the Jazz during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], Clarkson averaged 16.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. On March 27, 2025, Clarkson was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing a medical procedure to address [[plantar fasciitis]] in his left foot.{{Cite web|title=Jordan Clarkson Injury Update|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jordan-clarkson-injury-update|access-date=April 17, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On June 30, 2025, Clarkson reached a buyout agreement with the Jazz.{{Cite web|title=Utah Jazz and Jordan Clarkson Reach Buyout Agreement|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-and-jordan-clarkson-reach-buyout-agreement|access-date=June 30, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} ===New York Knicks (2025–present)=== On July 7, 2025, Clarkson signed with the [[New York Knicks]] on a minimum contract.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Jordan Clarkson expected to sign with Knicks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45624167/sources-jordan-clarkson-expected-sign-knicks|date=June 30, 2025|access-date=July 7, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-jordan-clarkson|title=NEW YORK KNICKS SIGN JORDAN CLARKSON|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2025|accessdate=July 11, 2025}} In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Clarkson helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}} He also became the first player of Filipino descent to win an NBA championship.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-how-jordan-clarkson-made-nba-history-by-winning-nba-championship|title=How Knicks’ Jordan Clarkson made NBA history by winning NBA championship|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/sports/basketball/991387/nba-jordan-clarkson-becomes-first-filipino-american-nba-champion/story/|title=NBA: Jordan Clarkson becomes first Filipino-American NBA champion|website=gmanetwork.com|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}} On July 10, 2026, Clarkson re-signed with the Knicks on a minimum contract.{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2026 |title=NEW YORK KNICKS RE-SIGN JORDAN CLARKSON |url=https://knicks.com/news/new-york-knicks-re-sign-jordan-clarkson |access-date=July 10, 2026 |website=knicks.com |language=en}} ==National team career== [[File:Bongbong Marcos in Dominican Republic v Philippines FBWC 2.jpg|thumb|right|Clarkson (#6) and other members of the [[Philippine men's national basketball team|Philippine national team]] pose with Philippine president [[Bongbong Marcos]]]] In 2011, talks were initiated for Clarkson to play for the [[Philippine men's national basketball team|Philippine national team]], also known as ''Gilas Pilipinas'' (loosely translated, "Prowess Philippines").{{cite web | url=http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/fibaworldcup/articles/378605/gilas-pilipinas-coach-chot-reyes-hits-out-at-asian-games-for-barring-andray-blatche | title=Gilas Pilipinas coach Chot Reyes hits out at Asian Games for barring Andray Blatche | work=GMA News Online | date=September 10, 2014 | access-date=February 6, 2015}} However, Clarkson did not meet the [[FIBA eligibility rules|FIBA eligibility]] requirements to be considered a Filipino citizen as he acquired his Philippine passport after age 16. He is eligible, though, to play as a "naturalized" player.{{cite web |agency=Agence France-Presse |title=Gilas Pilipinas to 'do everything' to have Jordan Clarkson for Fiba World Cup |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/339682/gilas-pilipinas-to-do-everything-to-have-jordan-clarkson-for-2019-fiba-world-cup-china |website=sports.inquirer.net |date=February 25, 2019 |access-date=February 25, 2019 |language=en}} Clarkson visited the Philippines in August 2015 on the invitation of [[Manny Pangilinan]], the then-president of [[Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas]] (SBP), the national basketball federation of the Philippines, to observe the training of ''Gilas'', aside from fulfilling his commitments as an endorser of [[Smart Communications]], which was also presided by Pangilinan.{{cite web | url=http://www.tribune.net.ph/sports/clarkson-to-help-gilas-shoot-for-olympic-slot| title=Clarkson to help Gilas shoot for Olympic slot | newspaper=The Daily Tribune | author=Julius Manicad|archive-date=December 22, 2015| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222010101/http://www.tribune.net.ph/sports/clarkson%2Dto%2Dhelp%2Dgilas%2Dshoot%2Dfor%2Dolympic%2Dslot|access-date=August 24, 2015}} In an interview, SBP Executive Director [[Sonny Barrios]] confirmed that Clarkson has carried a [[Philippine passport]] since he was 12, and therefore did not need to undergo the naturalization process to represent the Philippines in international competitions.{{cite web| url=http://cnnphilippines.com/sports/2015/08/24/Gilas-Pilipinas-Jordan-Clarkson-natural-born.html| title=SBP: No need to naturalize Jordan Clarkson| publisher=CNN Philippines| author=Paolo del Rosario| access-date=August 24, 2015| archive-date=October 13, 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013125419/http://cnnphilippines.com/sports/2015/08/24/Gilas-Pilipinas-Jordan-Clarkson-natural-born.html| url-status=dead}} Clarkson did not make the final cut due to scheduling conflicts with the Los Angeles Lakers. The Lakers agreed to let Clarkson play, but the [[NBA collective bargaining agreement]] requires that national team play should not interfere with the Lakers' team requirements, which expected players to report on September 28; however, the tournament ran until October 3.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2563000-jordan-clarkson-left-off-gilas-pilipinas-2015-fiba-asia-championship-roster|title=Jordan Clarkson Left off Gilas Pilipinas 2015 FIBA Asia Championship Roster|first=Mike |last=Chiari|website=[[Bleacher Report]] }} Clarkson expressed his disappointment that he could not represent the Philippines in the [[2015 FIBA Asia Championship]].{{cite web|url=http://pba.inquirer.net/60436/jordan-clarkson-statement-on-missing-gilas-fiba-asia-stint|title=Jordan Clarkson statement on missing Gilas' Fiba Asia stint|work=INQUIRER.net|date=September 9, 2015}} Clarkson was initially included in the 17-man pool for the Philippines lineup for the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|final Olympic Qualifying Tournament]] for the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics|2016 Rio Olympics]].[http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/gilas-pilipinas-pool-for-olympic-wildcard-qualifier-bared-castro-fajardo-lead-17-man-list Gilas Pilipinas pool for Olympic wildcard qualifier bared; Castro, Fajardo lead 17-man list] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016013841/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/gilas-pilipinas-pool-for-olympic-wildcard-qualifier-bared-castro-fajardo-lead-17-man-list |date=October 16, 2015 }} However, due to time constraints and a complicated eligibility process, the team instead opted for [[Andray Blatche]] as its naturalized player due to lack of size.{{cite web|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/sports/04/12/16/clarkson-wont-join-gilas-for-olympic-qualifiers|title=Clarkson won't join Gilas for Olympic qualifiers|author=|date=April 12, 2016}} In August 2018, the NBA cleared Clarkson to play for the Philippine national team in the [[Basketball at the 2018 Asian Games|2018 Asian Games]] that was held from August 18 to September 2, 2018, with a one-time exception, allowing Clarkson to play for the Philippines for the first time.{{cite web |title=Change of plans, NBA clears Jordan Clarkson to play in Asian Games |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/change-plans-nba-clears-jordan-115944745.html |website=sports.yahoo.com |access-date=August 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817135634/https://sports.yahoo.com/change-plans-nba-clears-jordan-115944745.html|archive-date=August 17, 2018}} His first game with the national team was against [[China men's national basketball team|China]] where Clarkson led all scorers with 28 points but fell short of the match 82–80.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.ph/basketball/gilas/story/_/id/24433394/jordan-clarkson-scores-28-gilas-pilipinas-loses-china|title=Clarkson scores 28 but Gilas Pilipinas loses to China|date=August 21, 2018}} In his second game with the national team, Clarkson once again led his team with a 25-point performance but could not overcome Korea. The team bowed out of a podium finish.{{cite web|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/sports/08/27/18/asian-games-south-korea-knocks-out-jordan-clarkson-philippines|title=Asian Games: South Korea knocks out Jordan Clarkson, Philippines|author=|date=August 27, 2018}} Clarkson managed to get his first win with the national team, defeating [[Japan men's national basketball team|Japan]] 113–80, in which he recorded 22 points, six rebounds and nine assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.ph/basketball/gilas/story/_/id/24499668/gilas-pilipinas-pounds-japan-moves-playoff-5th-place|title=Gilas Pilipinas pounds Japan, moves on to playoff for 5th place|date=August 28, 2018}} Clarkson ended the tournament with a win, beating [[Syria men's national basketball team|Syria]] 109–55 with a 29-point performance earning the Philippines a fifth-place finish, its best in 16 years.{{cite web |last1=Go |first1=Beatrice |title=Gilas drubs Syria for 5th place Asiad finish |url=https://www.rappler.com/sports/210852-results-basketball-philippines-vs-syria-game-august-31-2018/ |website=Rappler |access-date=December 24, 2019 |date=August 31, 2018}} In August 2022, SBP announced that they have accepted Clarkson as a naturalized player for the fourth window of the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 World Cup]] Asian qualifiers and future FIBA tournaments.{{cite web |last1=Agcaoili |first1=Lance |title=Jordan Clarkson can only play in Fiba tournaments as Gilas' naturalized player, says SBP |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/472832/jordan-clarkson-can-only-play-in-fiba-tournaments-as-gilas-naturalized-player-says-sbp |website=INQUIRER.net |access-date=January 18, 2023 |language=en |date=August 9, 2022}} On August 25, 2022, Clarkson made his FIBA debut and scored 27 points in a loss against [[Lebanon men's national basketball team|Lebanon]] in the FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers.{{Cite web |title=Breaking down Jordan Clarkson's post-game banter with Lebanon and FIBA debut |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/asian-qualifiers/news/breaking-down-jordan-clarkson-s-post-game-banter-with-lebanon-and-fiba-debut |access-date=August 27, 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=August 26, 2022 |language=en}} Clarkson was included in the 21-man pool for the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/fiba/the-21-man-gilas-pool-for-2023-fiba-world-cup-a795-20230606|title=Clarkson, Brownlee, Kouame head 21-man Gilas pool for World Cup|website=spin.ph|last=Terrado|first=Reuben|date=June 6, 2023|access-date=September 9, 2023}} where he was eventually included in the final 12-man lineup as the team's [[FIBA eligibility rules#Naturalized players|naturalized player]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/basketball/gilas/story/_/id/38243263/gilas-pilipinas-confirm-final-12-fiba-world-cup|title=Gilas Pilipinas confirm final 12 for FIBA World Cup|website=[[ESPN.com]]|last=Ventura|first=Sid|date=August 23, 2023|access-date=October 12, 2023}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/fiba/jordan-clarkson-commits-to-play-for-gilas-at-world-cup-a2244-20230725|title=SBP secures Jordan Clarkson commitment to play for Gilas at World Cup|website=spin.ph|last=Sayson|first=Homer|date=July 25, 2023|access-date=October 12, 2023}} In conclusion of the 2023 FIBA World Cup, he played 5 games for the Philippines averaging 26.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 5.2 assists, 1.2 steals, 0.2 blocks in 36 minutes of playing.{{Cite web|title=Jordan CLARKSON (PHI)'s profile - FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 - FIBA.basketball|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/player/Jordan-Clarkson|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=July 7, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
